newsitem.title: USA: BRENT CRUDE TRADES THINLY IN U.S. AFTERMARKET.
newsitem.headline: BRENT CRUDE TRADES THINLY IN U.S. AFTERMARKET.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude oil traded thinly in the U.S. aftermarket on Monday, traders said.
Three exchange-for-physical (EFP) deals were transacted for a total of 450 lots. Two were done at $18.54 and one at $18.56 a barrel.
Cash talk was subdued. September Brent closed at $18.58 a barrel on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE).
Three September/October spreads were dealt, all at minus 15 cents a barrel, at the high end of the day's earlier range of minus 18/15 cents.
